#1 Hi, all.

I am confused by the following sentence from the document here

In page 1249, The paper says:

By Theorem 3, 2op≅22^{\mathrm{op}}\cong 22op≅2

Theorem 3 says “any generator with exactly three endomorphisms is isomorphic to 222”, therefore, to show 2op≅22^{\mathrm{op}}\cong 22op≅2, there are two things to check: 1. 2op2^{\mathrm{op}}2op is a generator, 2. there are exactly three functors 2op→2op2^{\mathrm{op}} \to 2^{\mathrm{op}}2op→2op.

I agree that the axioms (Aop)op=A(A^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}} = A(Aop)op=A and (Fop)op=F(F^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}} = F(Fop)op=F makes sure that there is a one-to-one correspondence from functors A→BA \to BA→B to functors Aop→BopA^{\mathrm{op}} \to B^{\mathrm{op}}Aop→Bop. My confusion is to show the first point, that is, why is 2op2^{\mathrm{op}}2op a generator? That is, given functors f,g:A→Bf,g:A\to Bf,g:A→B such that f≠g f \neq gf=g, how can we come up with a functor a:2op→Aa:2^{\mathrm{op}} \to Aa:2op→A such that f∘a≠g∘af\circ a \neq g \circ af∘a=g∘a?

The author does not say anything like “we have an isomorphism 2→2op2\to 2^{\mathrm{op}}2→2op”, and the paper does not assume any “extensionality of categories” (i.e., we are not able to say two categories are equal iff they have equal collection of objects and a equal collection of arrows), therefore, the assumption (Aop)op=A(A^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}} = A(Aop)op=A does not really say anything about the objects an arrows of AopA^{\mathrm{op}}Aop, since the operation is applied on AAA, not on its object (which are defined to be functors 1→A1\to A1→A), and not on its arrows (which are defined to be functors 2→A2\to A2→A). Also note that this sentence is stated before assuming 1=1op1 = 1^{\mathrm{op}}1=1op and 2=2op2 = 2^{\mathrm{op}}2=2op, instead, the workflow seems to be: the axioms are sufficient to prove 2≅2op2\cong 2^{\mathrm{op}}2≅2op, and since assuming 2=2op2 = 2^{\mathrm{op}}2=2op does not break consistency, we can add this assumption.

Or is the author sloppy here with the “minor detail”? If so, I think I am in trouble. Any hint to fix this point?

Thanks to any attempt to help!
subject: Duality in McLarty's Axiomatization of CCAF
